project.name: Cotton Grade
project.title: Progressive Domain-Adaptive Transfer Learning for Fine-Grained Cotton Cultivar Identification
project.research_question: Does progressive cotton-domain adaptation improve final cultivar recognition compared with direct ImageNet transfer?
project.hypothesis: A backbone progressively adapted from generic ImageNet features to cotton-specific leaf and seed representations may learn more useful texture and morphology features before final fine-tuning on limited raw cotton fibre data.
project.deployment_note: Leaf and seed classifiers are completed training stages only. Production inference will load only the final raw-cotton model after the final stage is trained.

datasets.name: Cotton Leaf Image Dataset for Disease Classification
datasets.label_type: Alternaria Leaf Spot / Bacterial Blight / Fusarium Wilt / Healthy Leaf / Verticillium Wilt
datasets.source_scope: 1,373 original RGB images were ingested. Exact-duplicate cleaning retained 1,124 unique, non-conflicting labelled images for Cotton Grade.
datasets.purpose: Move ImageNet features into a real cotton-leaf visual domain and learn cotton morphology, disease patterns and fine surface texture before seed adaptation.

datasets.name: Cotton Seed Quality Dataset — 450-image evaluation set
datasets.source_scope: The paper reports 4,419 cropped seed images for model development; Cotton Grade uses the publicly downloadable 450-image S1 evaluation set (150 per class).
datasets.purpose: Further specialize the leaf-adapted backbone toward compact cotton structures, local texture, boundaries and surface irregularities.

datasets.name: CATGO Egyptian Cotton Fibre Dataset
datasets.source_scope: Candidate final target dataset; access and final training are still pending.
datasets.purpose: Final target domain for cultivar classification from RGB photographs of actual ginned cotton fibre.

stage_results.caveat: The source provides no sample_id metadata, so the reported split is stratified at image level. Before splitting, 199 same-class duplicate copies and 50 ambiguous cross-class images from 25 exact-duplicate groups were excluded.

The downloadable S1 evaluation set has no sample_id metadata, so the reported split is stratified at image level. Audit found zero corrupt files and zero exact duplicates. Average-hash near-duplicate flags were not treated as proof of duplication because the controlled seed images have highly similar framing and backgrounds.

experiment_routes.label: Direct baseline
experiment_routes.question: How strong is conventional ImageNet transfer learning on the final task?

experiment_routes.label: Leaf transfer
experiment_routes.question: Does cotton-specific leaf adaptation improve the final classifier?

experiment_routes.label: Seed transfer
experiment_routes.question: Does seed-domain adaptation improve fine texture recognition on lint?

experiment_routes.label: Progressive transfer
experiment_routes.question: Does the full progressive cotton-domain sequence outperform direct transfer?

rules: Use the exact same final train/validation/test specimen split across every transfer route.
Fit calibration on validation data only; never tune on the final test set.
Never split augmented views of the same source image or physical specimen across partitions.
Do not publish placeholder or mock metrics as experimental results.
Intermediate leaf and seed metrics must be disclosed as image-level evaluations because their public sources do not provide specimen identifiers.
